subject: Electrical Engineering
title: The Feedback Loop
description: A fast breakdown of The Feedback Loop for builders.

hook.text: A feedback loop connects a system's output back to its input — creating a self-correcting cycle.

buildup.text: The sensor measures output. The comparator finds the error. The controller decides the action.

discovery.text: Negative feedback reduces error and stabilizes. Positive feedback amplifies it and can cause runaway.

twist.text: Microphone feedback squeal is positive feedback — sound loops through speaker and mic, growing louder.

climax.text: Biology uses feedback too — body temperature, blood sugar, and heart rate are all regulated by loops.

punchline.text: Negative feedback stabilizes. Positive feedback explodes.

quiz.question: What does negative feedback do in a control system?
options: It amplifies the output until it saturates
It reduces error by counteracting deviations from the setpoint
It shuts down the system when an error is detected
